cities.d: Estonia's easternmost and third largest city, on the Narva River, which is the border with Russia. Famous for the Hermann Castle, right opposite Ivangorod's castle, and the Kreenholm factories.

hidden.d: Erected in 1668-1671, German, Swedish and Italian architectural influences are mixed in the building style of the Town Hall. The design stems from Georg Teuffel, a former architect from Lübeck.
Built in 1881-84 by Otto Hippius, who also constructed the Sangaste Castle in South Estonia, the building represents historicism with elements of classicism.

The gallery is the art centre of East-Viry County. It is located in an 18th-century ammunition warehouse. In addition to the permanent collection, exhibitions of modern Estonian and Western European art are organized and a…

It was built in 1890-1896 for the Orthodox Christian workers of Kreenholm Manufactory. The architectural style comes from Byzantine tradition. You can see three part iconostasis and 17th century’s crucifix of Christ.
The famous Kreenholm Textile Factory was built on the shore of the waterfall in the 19th century, and was the largest factory in the Russian Empire at that time.

n.en: Kreenholm area and Kreenholm Textile Factory

hidden.d: This is Narva’s oldest part, an example of park architecture from the end of the 19th century. You might be surprised what that just means.

x.intro: Narva is the easternmost city in Estonia, at the Russian border.

must.d: Founded at the end of the 13th century by the Danes. In 1347, the Danish king sold Northern Estonia to the Livonian Order. After that the castle was turned into a convent with a massive tower named Hermann.
Seven bastions were built in the 17th century: Victoria, Honor, Gloria, Fama, Triumph, Fortuna, and Spes. Work has been started to dry and light the bastions.

next.d: A small resort town at the mouth of the river Narva, 14 km northwest.
A beautiful coastal town in the east and formerly closed city with the best ensemble of Stalinist architecture in the entire Baltics.
Estonia's fifth largest city, west-wards, famous for its Punk and Rock festivals and spirit.
More than halfway to Tartu is this small and relaxing fishing village.
Museum-rich and Hanseatic city on the banks of the Emajõgi River. Also, Estonia's second-largest and oldest city, intellectual hub famous for its universities, and a lively student city.
On the coast within an hour east (50 km) of Tallinn. Given its size it is the largest park in Estonia and one of Europe's biggest national parks, with 1000 km2 of bogs, trails, and forests.
The financial and cosmopolitan centre of Estonia. Beautiful and expensive.

x.safe: While Estonia is generally very safe, Narva systematically ranks as the country's most dangerous place. Most murders, aggravated assaults, robberies, and car thefts in Estonia occur here.

cities.d: Estonia's fourth largest city and summer capital, popular for its balneotherapy complexes and spa centres, surrounded by numerous beaches.

hidden.d: The Town Hall is located in a house built in 1797 by the merchant P.R. Harder. In 1804, the Russian czar Alexander I stayed in this house during his visit to Pärnu.
Known to be the oldest building in Pärnu. It was built in 1658 on the remains of the old almshouse of the Holy Spirit's Church as a shelter to the sick and the cripples.

x.intro: Pärnu is a resort seaside city (and Estonia's summer capital) with a small harbour in south-western Estonia. The city is known for its spas, shallow white sandy beach and beautiful parks. In summer, Pärnu offers beach life, dozens of festivals, night clubs, big party crowds, concerts and funfairs.

next.d: Village with large beaches and an amusement park.

The southernmost group of islands, Kihnu, is on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Cosy and warm yet exotic – folk costumes are worn here every day and the handicraft of older generations remains highly…
The communal territory corresponds to that of the homonymous island, formerly known as Runö.
A quiet seaside village on the Gulf of Riga with bird-ringing centre and rural beaches.

The border is about 60 km south of Pärnu. Even more sand beaches, interesting castles in the cities of Cēsis and Sigulda, plus of course the Latvian capital Riga with things to see and do for several…

cities.d: Estonia's fifth largest city, east of Tallinn, famous for its punk and rock festivals and spirit.

x.around: The major landmark is the castle and its mountain, which stretches from north to south, along Pikk Street to the west – the most historic part of the city. The central square (Turu plats) is located in a couple of blocks to the east.

hidden.d: Trout farming in the northern outskirts of Halyal (10 km from Rakvere to the north). Fishing in the pond (hire fishing rods and selling food, as well as a free opportunity to dig worms for fishing).

A monument of a bizarre composition of architectural styles and the recklessness of the architect. Likely from the 19th century, when it was more or less a typical building in the spirit of classicism.
The pride of the locals. It is believed that Rakvere is the smallest city in the world, which has its own theatre and theatrical company.
The next point is not far from the former, just east of Simuna along the road to Paasvere there's a little stone pillar in the field marking the end of the Simuna line.
The original church was a two-storey building purchased according to an order of the Russian Emperor Nicholas I and the Most Holy Synod in 1839.

n.en: Orthodox Church of the Nativity of Theotokos

hidden.d: In the middle of a field next to the Ebavere-Simuna road stands the only building left of the Võivere manor. It's a windmill that served as a triangulation point and has now been restored into a visitors' centre.
From a distance this building resembles a workshop. In fact, it is a church built in the late 1930s in the style of radical radicalism.

x.intro: Rakvere (Tarbapea in ancient Estonian, Weisenberg in German, Rakowor in Russian) is Estonia’s fifth largest city and situated the northern part of the country, 20 km south of the Gulf of Finland and approximately 100 km east of Tallinn and west of Narva.

must.d: A nice manor house in the style of eclecticism, built between 1881-82.

This manor consists of a one-storey building, decorated with a luxurious portico in the style of classicism from 1820, including technical buildings of the same period; the barn and the stable have been preserved.
A manor house in the style of neoclassicism (end of the 19th century), and a very nice distillery, carelessly built of huge cobblestones. In addition, a small park completes the surroundings.
A brick building in the style of neoclassicism, built in 1850. Inside a collection of paintings and objects of everyday life can be found. When agreed with the owner, a look inside is possible.

The manor house slowly wilts. The interest part is a stone barn of the 18th century with five semicircular arches. The building is unexpectedly large and carefully designed from an architectural point of view.

One of the largest estates in this part of Estonia. In addition to the majestic house in the neoclassicism style, there are numerous official buildings, a huge park and a windmill in the form of a bottle.
A large manor house with a central building in the spirit of classicism. In addition, there is a landscape park with ponds and a war memorial of 1812.

next.d: The capital, and financial and cosmopolitan centre of Estonia, with a medieval Old Town. Beautiful and expensive.
The capital of the county, but rather uninteresting from a travellers point of view.
A coastal village inside of Lahemaa National Park.
A coastal small borough inside of Lahemaa National Park.
Estonia's eastern-most and third largest city, on the Narva River, which is the border with Russia. Famous for the Hermann castle, right opposite of the Ivangorod's castle, and the Kreenholm…

cities.d: the "Venice of the north" is a major seaside resort and port city, good for visiting spas, taking mud baths, sailing, and swimming.

x.around: Walking can be an option, but some destinations might be too far for walking.

hidden.d: Cyrillus Kreek (1889-1962) is known as the composer of choral works and was beloved by the people of Haapsalu. The permanent exposition introduces the composer's life and works.
The timber-laced Resort Hall and the Bandstand on the seaside Promenade were built at the end of the 19th century and are the only ones of the kind that have survived in their original form.
Built by former Soviet Union army Kiltsi airfield extends to ca 800 ha area. Concrete runways are 2500 m long, for the airplanes there were 28 hangars.
The museum is located in the former Town Hall in Lossiplatsi Square. Wander through the historic interior and learn about the old times of Haapsalu.
Communication Museum offers a review of the development of telecommunications in Western Estonia.

The ruins of the Ungru manor used to represent one of the most impressive Neo-Baroque buildings in Estonia, although it was never really finished. The contrasting Soviet airfield remains next to the manor.
The spa specializes in Thalasso treatments, the basic elements of which are sea mud, seawater, sea scent and sea nutrition present in various treatments.
The Haapsalu Shawl, an extremely fine knitted shawl that can be pulled through a woman's ring, has been the symbol of Haapsalu since the last century.

x.intro: Haapsalu is a major seaside resort town on the west coast of Estonia, approximately 100 km south-west of Tallinn.

must.d: The Haapsalu Bishop’s Castle and Cathedral, which was established in the 13th century as the centre of the Saare-Lääne Diocese, is one of the best preserved castles in Estonia.

next.d: Estonia's 4th largest city and the summer capital of Estonia, popular for its balneo-therapy complexes and spa centres, surrounded by numerous beaches.
A bilingual municipality: Estonian and Swedish. Step into Swedish and Soviet history.
The second largest Estonian island. Popular for its lighthouses, ancient churches, historical values and the sense of humour of its inhabitants, but scarcely populated.
The largest Estonian and wild seaside character island with castles and fortresses, one perfectly preserved, a beach, a spa and famous mills. Saaremaa is even sometimes called Sparemaa.

cities.d: The only town on the island of Saaremaa, the location of Kuressaare Castle. It also has many spas, water parks, and a beach.

hidden.d: The fortress is well preserved and located in the city center.

The spa and sauna center features a swimming pool, cold water pool and Japanese pool, small children’s pool, jacuzzi and foot baths, 2 steam baths, juniper sauna, Finnish sauna, birch sauna, aroma sauna, salt room, Garra Rufa…

x.intro: Kuressaare is the capital of Saaremaa, the largest of Estonia's islands.

next.d: Estonia's 4th largest city and the summer capital of Estonia, popular for its balneo-therapy complexes and spa centres, surrounded by numerous beaches.
Estonia's second largest island.

intro: Estonia (Estonian: Eesti) is a Baltic gem offering visitors the chance to see a tiny dynamic land on the shores of the sea. The northernmost and smallest of the Baltic states, Estonia has charming old towns and heritage back to the Hanseatic League. Tallinn's old town was built in the Middle Ages, but is in magnificent condition, with the city walls and towers almost completely intact, and it rates as one of Europe's best medieval old towns.

other.d: On the coast within an hour east (50 km) of Tallinn. Given its size it is the largest park in Estonia and one of Europe's biggest national parks, with 1,000 km2 of bogs, trails, and forests.

x.around: If you came here for hiking then by foot will be your preferred option.

hidden.d: The manor is in the village of the same name, directly on the road. It has a rich history. Since the 13th century there was a fortress, which was destroyed in the Livonian War.
A small cemetery church built in the middle of the 19th century. If you are lucky enough to get inside, pay attention to the huge and rather modernist picture of the Crucifix in the altar.
Not in Lahemaa National Park but at its border, and larger and more diverse than Viru raba. A huge bog with countless water pools and also a wooden plank trails over the swamp.

One of the most suggested place to go there is Viru raba, which has a foot track and observation tower. You can start and finish in same location if you go to the tower and back (2 km) or take a round trip around the swamp (5…
Perhaps, this is one of the most interesting Estonian estates. It does not have a luxurious palace - on the contrary, both manor houses are small and rather modest.
An 18th-century manor house and its park, and one of the most prominent and grand baroque manor buildings in Estonia.
Boulders in Lahemaa are everywhere, but in Käsmu they are especially numerous and huge. Each large boulder has its own name, indicated on the park's maps placed here and there.
The northernmost point/peninsula of mainland Estonia is a stony spit that stands out almost 1 km into the sea. It is about 4 km from Viinistu.

x.intro: Lahemaa National Park (Estonian: Lahemaa rahvuspark) is a national park in North Estonia. It was the first national park to be created in the now dissolved Soviet Union.

next.d: some 20 km east of Tallinn, this is Estonia's largest waterfall. It is better to go early in the morning to catch the soft dawn light or in the evening when the sun shines on the falls.
Estonia's fifth largest city, east of Tallinn, famous for its Punk and Rock festivals and spirit.
The capital, and financial and cosmopolitan centre of Estonia, with a medieval Old Town. Beautiful and expensive.

x.safe: In these forest there is a great possibility of catching a tick that can carry a disease (TBC or ehrlichia or borreliosis). Therefore a sufficient repellent is highly suggested. Also it is recommended to wear long, light clothes and examine your body in the evening to find any ticks.

other.d: one of the largest and most important autumn stopping grounds for migratory birds in Europe. Excellent for birdwatchers, due it is rich ornithological species.

x.around: You can explore the landscape on foot, by bicycle or by boat (to Matsalu Bay).
x.intro: Matsalu National Park is in Läänemaa county, western Estonia.

next.d: "Venice of the north", and a major seaside resort and medium-sized port city, good for visiting spas, taking mud baths, sailing and swimming.

other.d: the hilly landscapes of Southern Estonia. Estonia’s smallest national park between Valga and Võru.

next.d: A small town set in the hills of south Estonia and best known winter sports centre in the Baltics, and the Winter Capital of Estonia. Surrounded by lakes, hills and ski jump towers.
A town on the border with Latvia, where it literally grows into the Latvian town of Valka. Just to the west.
A picturesque town not far from the highest hill in the Baltic states, Suur Munamägi. The birthplace of the writer Kreutzwald and the dialect of the Estonian language. Just to the east.

other.d: Part of the Otepää recreational region with an area beyond 3,000 km². Trails along the lake and paths in the hilly forests.

x.around: Walking is the best option in the centre. To get to the lake or ski area, you better take the bus.

hidden.d: Hike along the paths of the park.
Rental of snowboards, cross-country skis, snow scooters and other winter sports equipment. Friendly and efficient owner who can provide information on snow and ice conditions.
The place has a mechanical lift allowing to go down slopes on a kind of plastic buoy. The track is sometimes artificially snowed.
Neo-Gothic and 51 m in height. Constructed in 1671, and repaired in 1850 including a new choir balcony. The pipe organ was built in 1852 in Tartu by Kessler. The church tower was built in 1860.

n.en: Monument of the visit of Dalai-Lama

hidden.d: This place includes a Golden Ratio Stone Spiral, a Chartres Labyrinth, and a tepee – a conical tent. Labyrinths have been used for gaining energy and walking meditation.
Beautiful views from observation towers on top of Harimägi hill. 28 m height in total, with the highest platform at 24 m.

Open-air concerts are held in completely natural venues on the hilly landscapes of the Otepää highland. The musicians' stage is on an island in the lake, surrounded by thousands of listeners on the sloping shore.

x.intro: Otepää is a small town with 2,000 inhabitants set in the hills of south Estonia, approximately 50 km south from Tartu.

must.d: Part of the Otepää recreational region with an area of ​​2,859 km². Trails along the lake provide access to the banks and picnic areas. It is possible to rent a boat to reach the islands on the lake, which are uninhabited.
Observe the ruins of the bishop's castle. The hill (165.6 m NN) emerged about 13,000 years ago during the Ice Age. Then, 1000 years ago the most important castle in ancient Ugala was built here.

n.en: Otepää Town Hill and Bishop's Castle ruins

next.d: Museum-rich and hanseatic city on the banks of the Emajõgi River. Also, Estonia's second-largest and oldest city, intellectual hub famous for its universities, and a lively student city.
A town on the border with Latvia, where it literally grows into the Latvian town of Valka.
A beautiful, ancient and hilly city, known for its annual Viljandi Folk Music Festival, beautiful old town and overwhelming and picturesque park around the old castle.
A picturesque town not far from the highest hill in the Baltic states, Suur Munamägi. The birthplace of the writer Kreutzwald and the dialect of the Estonian language.

other.d: The largest Estonian and wild seaside character island with castles and fortresses, one perfectly preserved, a beach, a spa and famous mills. Saaremaa is even sometimes called Sparemaa.

x.around: Distances are moderate. A car or bicycle offers flexibility for remote nature spots. Local buses link towns and larger villages, though schedules can be sparse outside the peak season. Roads are generally in good condition; minor roads can be narrow.

hidden.d: Saaremaa’s largest bog. The study trail is about 4.8–5.7 km with information boards and several viewpoints. Some sections can be wet depending on season; waterproof footwear is recommended. Cranberries can be found in autumn.
The only remaining group of windmills on Saaremaa is in the village of Angla.

Behind the tiny village of Asva on a low-lying hayfield is one of the most archaeologically important Bronze-Age sites in Northern Europe. Asva has given its name to an entire culture. See Vikings and the Old Norse for context.
About 9 m high wooden tower along the study trail (≈1.5 km from the parking). Wide views over open bog, bog forest and pools. Stay on the boardwalk and follow local guidance.
It is the highest of the Saaremaa and Muhu cliffs, reaching to a maximum of 21.3 metres. The entire cliff is approximately 2.5 km long.

The most probable age of the Kaali craters is 7500-7600 years. Kaali lake is considered to be the most unique geological object in Estonia. Known as Holy Lake it also has an important place in tradition.

x.intro: Saaremaa is the largest Estonian island. It is on the west coast of Estonia. The capital (and only city) in Saaremaa is Kuressaare, which is covered in a separate article.

next.d: The second largest Estonian island. Popular for its lighthouses, ancient churches, historical values and the sense of humour of its inhabitants, but scarcely populated.
The third largest Estonian island, and a rural municipality connected to the nearby Saaremaa by an artificial embankment, where ferries to the harbour of Virtsu arrive.
Estonia's 4th largest city and the summer capital of Estonia, popular for its balneo-therapy complexes and spa centres, surrounded by numerous beaches.
Rich in marine fauna, and international bird sanctuary with over 250 recorded bird species, on the west coast of Saaremaa.

x.safe: Check weather conditions near cliffs and exposed coasts, especially in storms. Stay on marked trails in bogs and nature reserves. Ticks are present in warmer months—use repellent and check after hikes.
